mainTopic: שבת 75b: finishing the 39 מלאכות (צובע, מעבד, ממחק, מכה בפטיש, כותב/מוחק, the count of 39), and the new משנה on items fit to store for הוצאה
overview: This amud finishes רב's ruling that a שוחט is liable for צובע as well as נטילת נשמה, because the butcher wants the bloody neck to attract customers. The גמרא then goes through the משנה's list of מלאכות. It replaces the double-counted מולח/מעבד with שרטוט, and it debates whether salting meat counts as tanning. It gives everyday examples of ממחק, מחתך and מכה בפטיש, and a general rule that any finishing act is מכה בפטיש. A ברייתא shows that erasing one big letter can be stricter than writing one. The words 'אלו' and 'forty less one' are explained as rejecting רבי אליעזר and רבי יהודה. A new משנה then teaches that liability for carrying depends on whether an item is worth storing. The גמרא asks what 'fit to store' excludes, debating דם נדה and עצי אשרה. It notes that this standard does not follow רבי שמעון, and it then quotes the next clause, which is discussed on the next amud.

steps.title: Is the slaughterer only liable for dyeing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב's ruling. Saying a שוחט is liable 'for צובע' sounds like he is not liable for נטילת נשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For dyeing, yes, he is liable; for taking a life, no?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the way רב's earlier ruling (השוחט חייב משום צובע) was worded. It sounds as if killing the animal is not a problem at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering is obviously the מלאכה of נטילת נשמה, which is one of the 39 אבות מלאכה. So if רב only mentioned צובע, it sounds like he is denying the obvious liability, and that cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking a life, i.e., killing a living creature

phrases.english: Because of dyeing — yes,
phrases.notes: Refers back to רב's ruling that a שוחט is liable for dyeing.

phrases.english: because of taking a life — no?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. Of course killing is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם צוֹבֵעַ אִין, מִשּׁוּם נְטִילַת נְשָׁמָה לָא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that a שוחט is liable for צובע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning only צובע implies there is no liability for נטילת נשמה, which is clearly false.

steps.title: Liable for dyeing as well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording. He is liable for צובע in addition to נטילת נשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: he is liable also because of dyeing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the wording of רב's ruling. Add the word 'also.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב never meant to deny the killing liability. His new point is that there is a second, extra liability, for צובע, on top of נטילת נשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read it as), used to correct or reread a statement

phrases.english: Say: also because of dyeing.
phrases.notes: He gets two liabilities, one for killing and one for dyeing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's wording seemed to imply that the liability is only for צובע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The liability for צובע comes in addition to the liability for נטילת נשמה.

steps.title: רב explains why the dyeing is wanted
steps.stepSummary: רב defends his own ruling. The butcher actually wants the neck to look bloody so customers will see the meat is fresh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: About the statement I made, let me add an explanation, so that later generations will not come and laugh at me. How is the dyeing something he wants? He wants the slaughter area to be soaked with blood, so people will see it and come buy from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a reason to his ruling. He wants to head off the obvious objection that nobody slaughtering an animal wants to dye its neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מלאכה normally needs to be something the person wants. A careless side effect is not enough. רב shows that for a butcher, the bloody neck is a real benefit: it shows the meat is freshly slaughtered and brings in customers.

keyTerms.meaning: A word, a statement, a matter
It is pleasing or desirable to him
The place of slaughter on the neck

steps.whatToRemember: A שוחט is liable for both נטילת נשמה and צובע, because the butcher actually wants the bloody look on the neck.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea in הלכות שבת: a result counts as a מלאכה only when the person actually wants it.

phrases.english: Rav said:
The statement that I said, I will say an explanation about it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא לֵיתוּ דָּרֵי בָּתְרָאֵי וְלִיחֲכוּ עֲלַי:
phrases.english: so that later generations will not come and laugh at me:
Dyeing, in what way is it desirable to him?
He wants the slaughter area to be soaked with blood,
so that people will see it
and come to buy from him.
phrases.notes: The bloody neck advertises that the meat is fresh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the extra liability for צובע from step 2 makes sense.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dyeing of the neck is desirable to the butcher, so it counts as the מלאכה of צובע.

steps.title: Aren't salting and tanning the same thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of מולח and מעבד. It objects that salting is just one stage of tanning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And one who salts it and one who tans it.' But salting is the same as tanning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase in the משנה. It then challenges the list for counting the same מלאכה twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists exactly 39 separate אבות מלאכה. Salting a hide is part of the tanning process, so listing both seems to double-count one מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who tans (processes the hide into leather)

phrases.english: [Mishnah:] And one who salts it and one who tans it.
Salting is the same as tanning!

steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of both מולח and מעבד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Salting is part of tanning, so the list of 39 counts one מלאכה twice.

steps.title: Replace one of them with drafting lines
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say to remove one of the two and put שרטוט in its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both said: Take out one of them and put in drafting lines.
steps.whatsHappening: Two great אמוראים agree with the objection. They fix the list by swapping in a different מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They accept that מולח and מעבד are really one מלאכה. To keep the count at 39, they put in שרטוט, the marking of lines on the hide before cutting it.

keyTerms.meaning: Drawing guide lines (on the hide, before cutting)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why שרטוט is counted as one of the 39 מלאכות.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish both said:
Take out one of them and put in drafting lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the objection of step 4 and fixes the list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual replacement in the list of מלאכות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מולח and מעבד are two separate מלאכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: They count as one. שרטוט fills the empty place in the 39.

steps.title: Salting meat counts as tanning
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that salting meat makes one liable for מעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Someone who salts meat is liable because of tanning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from salting hides to salting food. רבה בר רב הונא says salting meat is a form of tanning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salting meat preserves it and changes its texture, much like salting a hide. So רבה בר רב הונא treats it as the מלאכה of מעבד, even though it is food.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable (to bring a קרבן חטאת, if done בשוגג)

phrases.english: Rabbah bar Rav Huna said:
One who salts meat —
is liable because of tanning.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salting meat falls under the מלאכה of מעבד.

steps.title: רבא: no tanning applies to food
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees and says the מלאכה of tanning never applies to food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There is no tanning with food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite view to רבה בר רב הונא. Food cannot be 'tanned.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, עיבוד is a category about hides and similar materials. Doing something to food, even preserving it with salt, does not fit into this category at all.

phrases.english: Rava said:
There is no tanning with foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבה בר רב הונא in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מלאכה of מעבד does not apply to food.

steps.title: רב אשי limits רבה בר רב הונא to travel food
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that even רבה בר רב הונא only meant heavy salting for a trip. Salting for home use is never tanning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even רבה בר רב הונא only said this when he needs the meat for a journey. But for home, a person does not turn his food into wood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי narrows how far apart the two views really are. He limits רבה בר רב הונא's ruling to one specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat packed for a long trip is salted very heavily until it becomes hard, almost like processed leather. That is the only case רבה בר רב הונא was talking about. Normal salting for meals at home leaves the food as food, so no one would call it tanning.
steps.whatToRemember: Salting meat is tanning only according to רבה בר רב הונא, and even then only when it is salted heavily for a trip. Salting for home use is not tanning according to anyone.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא לָא אָמַר
phrases.english: And even Rabbah bar Rav Huna only said it
where he needs it for a journey,
but for the house —
a person does not make his food into wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא לָא אָמַר אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רבה בר רב הונא (step 6) and narrows the dispute with רבא (step 7).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salting food for home use is not עיבוד according to anyone. The dispute concerns only heavy salting for travel.

steps.title: Smoothing the hide between pillars
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes ממחק and מחתך from the משנה. רבי אחא בר חנינא gives an example of ממחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And one who smooths it and one who cuts it.' רבי אחא בר חנינא said: One who rubs a hide between pillars on שבת is liable because of smoothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next pair of מלאכות in the משנה. It gives a practical example of ממחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ממחק means scraping or smoothing a hide to make its surface even. Rubbing a hide back and forth between posts made for that purpose smooths it, so it falls under this מלאכה.

phrases.english: [Mishnah:] And one who smooths it and one who cuts it.
Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said:
One who rubs [a hide] between the pillars on Shabbat —
is liable because of smoothing.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rubbing a hide between pillars is ממחק.

steps.title: Three rulings of רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports three rulings: planing posts is מחתך, spreading a bandage is ממחק, and chiseling a stone is מכה בפטיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: רב אשי told me three things in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי. One who planes the tops of posts on שבת is liable for cutting. One who spreads a bandage on שבת is liable for smoothing. One who chisels a stone on שבת is liable for striking with a hammer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings three more examples of these מלאכות. Each one is something people do in everyday life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planing posts to an exact, even height is precise cutting, so it is מחתך. Spreading ointment smoothly on a bandage evens out a surface, so it is ממחק. Chiseling the final shape of a stone finishes the object, so it is מכה בפטיש, the final blow that completes a piece of work.

keyTerms.meaning: A bandage or plaster with ointment
One who chisels or dresses stone
Striking with a hammer, the final finishing touch of any work

steps.confusionAlert: מכה בפטיש is not only about hammering. It is the general מלאכה of putting the finishing touch on any object.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים סָח לִי רַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Rav Ashi told me three things
in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
One who planes the tops of posts on Shabbat —
is liable because of cutting,
one who spreads a bandage on Shabbat —
is liable because of smoothing,
and one who chisels a stone on Shabbat —
is liable because of striking with a hammer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more practical cases of ממחק and מחתך, and introduces מכה בפטיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Planing posts is מחתך. Spreading a bandage is ממחק. Chiseling a stone is מכה בפטיש.

steps.title: Engraving a vessel and blowing glass
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that engraving a design on a vessel and blowing glass are both מכה בפטיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן קיסמא said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: One who engraves a figure on a vessel, or one who blows a glass vessel, is liable because of striking with a hammer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more examples of מכה בפטיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both acts complete the making of a vessel. Engraving adds the final decoration, and blowing gives the glass its finished shape. Finishing an object is exactly what מכה בפטיש covers.

keyTerms.meaning: One who engraves or forms a design

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Kisma said
that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
One who engraves a figure on a vessel
and one who blows a glass vessel —
is liable because of striking with a hammer.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Engraving a vessel and blowing glass are מכה בפטיש.

steps.title: Removing stray threads from a cloak
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that removing stray threads from a garment is מכה בפטיש, but only if the owner cares about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: One who removes stray threads from cloaks is liable because of striking with a hammer. This applies only when he is particular about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a clothing example of מכה בפטיש. It adds a condition that limits the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner would not wear the cloak with those threads sticking out, then removing them is what finishes the garment. If he does not care about them, the cloak is already complete, so removing them finishes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And this applies only (introduces a limitation)

steps.whyThisMatters: The person's own standards decide when an object counts as 'finished' for מכה בפטיש.

phrases.english: Rav Yehudah said:
One who removes stray threads from cloaks —
is liable because of striking with a hammer.
And this applies only when he is particular about them.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Removing stray threads is מכה בפטיש, but only when the owner cares about them.

steps.title: Writing versus erasing one large letter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes כותב שתי אותיות and brings a ברייתא. Writing one big letter is exempt, but erasing one big letter that leaves room for two is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And one who writes two letters.' The רבנן taught: If he wrote one large letter, and its space could fit two letters, he is exempt. If he erased one large letter, and its space could fit two letters, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the מלאכה of writing. It brings a ברייתא comparing writing and erasing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing is measured by the number of letters actually written, so one letter is not enough no matter how big it is. Erasing is measured by the space it clears for new writing, so clearing room for two letters is enough.
steps.confusionAlert: The size of the letter is the same in both cases. The difference is what each מלאכה measures: letters written for כותב, space cleared for מוחק.

phrases.english: [Mishnah:] And one who writes two letters.
The Sages taught:
If he wrote one large letter
and in its space there is room to write two — he is exempt.
If he erased a large letter,
and in its space there is room to write two — he is liable.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: One large letter written is exempt. One large letter erased, leaving room for two, is liable.

steps.title: Here erasing is stricter than writing
steps.stepSummary: רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי points out that in this case erasing is stricter than writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מנחם ברבי יוסי said: This is a stringency of erasing over writing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מנחם sums up the lesson of the ברייתא. Here the destructive act is treated more strictly than the creative one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually creating is the main part of a מלאכה and destroying is secondary. Here erasing is stricter, because erasing counts by the space cleared for writing, while writing needs two real letters.
steps.whatToRemember: Writing needs two actual letters. Erasing only needs to clear space for two letters. So in this case מוחק is stricter than כותב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Menachem son of Rabbi Yosei said:
This is a stringency of erasing over writing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the general lesson from the ברייתא in step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In this case מוחק is stricter than כותב, because erasing is measured by the space it clears for writing.

steps.title: Any finishing act counts as striking with a hammer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list ending with מכה בפטיש. רבה and רבי זירא then give a general rule: any act that completes a piece of work makes one liable for מכה בפטיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'One who builds, one who dismantles, one who extinguishes, one who kindles, and one who strikes with a hammer.' רבה and רבי זירא both said: anything that involves the completion of a piece of work makes one liable for striking with a hammer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה's list. It then gives one big rule that explains what מכה בפטיש really covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10-12 gave single examples of מכה בפטיש, such as chiseling a stone or blowing glass. Here רבה and רבי זירא give the general principle behind all of them. The final 'finishing touch' that makes an item ready to use is מכה בפטיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Striking with a hammer: the מלאכה of giving the final touch that finishes an item
Completion of the work: the finishing step

steps.whatToRemember: מכה בפטיש = any act that finishes an item and makes it ready to use.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the key for deciding many modern cases. Any final step that completes an object can fall under מכה בפטיש.

phrases.english: One who builds, and one who dismantles,
one who extinguishes, and one who kindles,
and one who strikes with a hammer.
Rabba and Rabbi Zeira both said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מִידֵּי דְּאִית בֵּיהּ גְּמַר מְלָאכָה
phrases.english: Anything that has in it completion of work
is liable for striking with a hammer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues going through the משנה's list. It moves to the last group of מלאכות and gives a general definition of מכה בפטיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any act that involves גמר מלאכה is liable under מכה בפטיש.

steps.title: The word 'these' rejects רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'these are the אבות מלאכות'. The word 'אלו' is meant to reject רבי אליעזר, who holds one is liable separately for a תולדה done together with its אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'These are the primary labors.' The word 'these' comes to exclude the view of רבי אליעזר. He makes a person liable for a sub-labor together with its main labor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה ends with the word 'these'. It is telling us that the list is closed, against רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says that if someone does both an אב and its תולדה in one lapse of awareness, he brings two קרבנות. Then the number of possible חטאות could go above 39. The word 'אלו' teaches that only these 39 count, so you can never bring more than 39.

keyTerms.meaning: The primary categories of forbidden labor on שבת
A sub-labor that comes from a primary labor
Together with (in the place of) the primary labor

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר agrees that a תולדה is forbidden like an אב. The argument is only whether doing both together brings two separate חטאות.

phrases.english: "These are the primary labors."
"These" comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Eliezer,
who makes one liable for a sub-labor together with its primary labor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the משנה's closing words and explains what they are meant to exclude.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'אלו' limits liability to the 39 אבות. This rejects רבי אליעזר's extra חטאת for a תולדה done together with its אב.

steps.title: 'Less one' rejects רבי יהודה's additions
steps.stepSummary: The number 'forty less one' is meant to reject רבי יהודה. A ברייתא shows that he adds two more מלאכות: שובט and מדקדק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Less one' comes to exclude the view of רבי יהודה. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה adds lining up the threads and beating the threads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה stresses the exact number 39. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה wanted to add more מלאכות. The reply to him comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה were right, the list would have 41 מלאכות. The exact count of 39 tells us his two additions are not separate אבות.

keyTerms.meaning: Lining up or straightening the warp threads
Beating the threads tight in weaving

phrases.english: "Less one" comes to exclude the view of Rabbi Yehuda,
as it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda adds
lining up the threads and beating the threads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'לאפוקי' pattern as Step 16, now applied to the number of מלאכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exact count of 39 rejects רבי יהודה's addition of שובט and מדקדק as separate אבות.

steps.title: The Sages fold the two additions into existing labors
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה. שובט is part of מיסך (setting up the warp), and מדקדק is part of אורג (weaving).
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: lining up is included in setting the warp, and beating is included in weaving.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's two extra מלאכות. They show that each one already belongs under a מלאכה on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not say these acts are allowed. They say they are not new categories, because they fit under existing אבות. That is why the total stays at 39.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting up the warp threads on the loom

steps.whatToRemember: There are exactly 39 אבות. Acts that seem new are often already included in an existing אב.
steps.confusionAlert: שובט and מדקדק are still forbidden on שבת. The argument is only about whether they count as separate categories.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: שׁוֹבֵט הֲרֵי הוּא בִּכְלַל מֵיסֵךְ,
phrases.english: They said to him: lining up is included in setting the warp,
beating is included in weaving.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: שׁוֹבֵט הֲרֵי הוּא בִּכְלַל מֵיסֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה from the ברייתא in Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects counting שובט and מדקדק as independent אבות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each act is really part of an existing מלאכה (מיסך or אורג), so it is not a new category.

steps.title: New משנה: liability depends on whether the item is worth storing
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that carrying out an item people usually store makes one liable for a חטאת. If people do not usually store such an item, only someone who personally stores it is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said another general rule: anything fit to be stored, and people store things like it, if one carried it out on שבת he is liable for a חטאת. Anything not fit to be stored, and people do not store things like it, if one carried it out on שבת, only the person who stores it is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a rule about the מלאכה of הוצאה (carrying out). It tells us which items are important enough to make one liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for carrying depends on whether the item matters. If people generally save it, carrying it is a real act. If people generally do not save it, it only matters to the one person who chose to save it. So he alone is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: To store or put away for later use
He carried it out (to another domain)
Sin-offering brought for an accidental violation

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that how important an item is, both in general and to the person, affects liability for הוצאה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And they stated another general rule:
anything fit to be stored, and people store things like it,
and he carried it out on Shabbat, he is liable for a sin-offering for it.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָּשֵׁר לְהַצְנִיעַ וְאֵין מַצְנִיעִין כָּמוֹהוּ
phrases.english: And anything not fit to be stored, and people do not store things like it,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוֹצִיאוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת — אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא הַמַּצְנִיעוֹ.
phrases.english: and he carried it out on Shabbat, only the one who stores it is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the list of 39 מלאכות is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying out an item normally stored makes everyone liable for a חטאת. An item not normally stored makes only the person who stores it liable.

steps.title: What does 'fit to store' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of item the words 'כשר להצניע' come to leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Anything fit to be stored': what does this come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the משנה's wording. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already says 'people store things like it'. So the extra words 'fit to store' must be there to rule out a specific kind of item. The גמרא wants to know which one.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to exclude?

phrases.english: GEMARA: "Anything fit to be stored"
comes to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which item is excluded by the phrase 'כשר להצניע'.

steps.title: Two answers: menstrual blood or idolatrous wood
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the phrase excludes דם נדה. מר עוקבא says it excludes עצי אשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it excludes menstrual blood. מר עוקבא said: it excludes wood of an אשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים each give a different example of an item that is not fit to store.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דם נדה seems useless to people. עצי אשרה is forbidden for any benefit, so it has no value. The next step explains whether each view also agrees with the other's example.

keyTerms.meaning: Wood of a tree worshipped as idolatry, forbidden for any benefit

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לְאַפּוֹקֵי דַּם נִדָּה.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: to exclude menstrual blood.

phrases.aramaic: מָר עֻוקְבָא אָמַר: לְאַפּוֹקֵי עֲצֵי אֲשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: Mar Ukva said: to exclude wood of an ashera.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: לְאַפּוֹקֵי דַּם נִדָּה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא: דם נדה. מר עוקבא: עצי אשרה.

steps.title: Explaining how far each view goes
steps.stepSummary: The view that excludes דם נדה surely also excludes עצי אשרה. The view that excludes only עצי אשרה holds that דם נדה is stored to feed a cat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said menstrual blood would certainly say אשרה wood too. The one who said אשרה wood holds that menstrual blood is stored to feed to the cat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the relationship between the two opinions. It shows that one view is broader than the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עצי אשרה must be destroyed, so it is clearly worthless. Anyone who calls דם נדה worthless would agree about the wood (כל שכן). מר עוקבא, however, sees a small use for the blood as cat food. So for him it is fit to store.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר דַּם נִדָּה, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן עֲצֵי אֲשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: The one who said menstrual blood, all the more so ashera wood.
The one who said ashera wood,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דַּם נִדָּה מַצְנַע לֵיהּ לְשׁוּנָּרָא.
phrases.english: but menstrual blood, one stores it for the cat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר דַּם נִדָּה, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן עֲצֵי אֲשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the two answers given in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא excludes both items. מר עוקבא excludes only עצי אשרה, because דם נדה has a use as cat food.

steps.title: What about the cat-food use?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב פפא deals with the point that דם נדה can be stored for a cat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other (רב פפא), what does he say to that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא with מר עוקבא's argument. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood can feed a cat, it seems to have some value. Then it should count as fit to store, and רב פפא's example would not work.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one: how does he answer?

phrases.english: And the other?
phrases.notes: A one-word question: how does רב פפא answer the cat argument?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns מר עוקבא's reasoning from Step 22 against רב פפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's view that דם נדה is not fit to store.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דם נדה has a use as cat food, so it seems fit to store.

steps.title: Feeding it to a cat weakens the woman, so no one stores it
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא holds that people do not store the blood for a cat. Doing so is believed to weaken the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it weakens her, people do not store it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא. People avoid feeding this blood to a cat, so they do not store it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The use is possible in theory, but people avoid it because they believe it harms the woman. Since no one actually stores it, the item stays 'not fit to store'.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Fit to store' depends on what people actually do. A possible use that people avoid does not make an item worth storing.

phrases.english: Since it weakens her,
one does not store it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical-behavior distinction: a possible use that people avoid does not count.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cat food is a real use, so דם נדה should count as fit to store.
steps.terutzMaskana: People avoid it because it weakens the woman, so it is not stored and remains unfit.

steps.title: The משנה's fixed measures do not follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא says our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון said the fixed measures were stated only for people who store these items.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: This משנה is not like רבי שמעון. If it were like רבי שמעון, there would be a problem, because he said: The חכמים only gave all these measures for the people who store those items.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא tells us whose opinion our משנה follows. It is not רבי שמעון's, because רבי שמעון ties the measures to the person who stores the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה gives one fixed measure for everyone: what is fit to store and how much makes a person חייב. רבי שמעון says these measures were stated only for people who actually store such things, so the person matters. Since the משנה uses one general standard instead, it cannot match רבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not like... (the opinion of)
But didn't he say...? (pointing to a known statement)
Fixed measures or minimum amounts that make a person liable

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'לא אמרו... אלא' is not a denial that the measures exist. It means the measures were stated only for one group: the people who store these items.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic difference in how to measure liability for carrying. The question is whether there is one standard for everyone, or whether it depends on how the particular person treats the item.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
This is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the fixed measures of our משנה.

phrases.english: for if it were in accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
didn't he say:
They did not state all these measures
phrases.notes: 'They' means the חכמים of the משנה.

phrases.english: except for those who store them.
phrases.notes: The measures are tied to people who actually store such items.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא הַאי דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing what 'כשר להצניע' leaves out, the גמרא now says which תנא the משנה's fixed measures follow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's objective, fixed measures do not follow רבי שמעון. He holds that the measures were stated only for those who store such items.

steps.title: Quoting the next phrase of the משנה: anything not fit to store
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה, 'And anything not fit to store,' to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'And anything that is not fit to store.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next words of the משנה. This is a setup line that prepares the next discussion of this phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the משנה turns to items too unimportant for people to normally store. The משנה teaches that for such items, only someone who did store them is חייב for carrying them out. The גמרא brings up the phrase now so it can examine it next.

keyTerms.meaning: To store away, to put aside for later use

phrases.english: And anything that is not fit to store.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, introducing the next topic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of 'כשר להצניע' and whose view it follows, the גמרא moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה's clause about items not fit to store. Only one who stores such an item is liable for carrying it out.
